answer: One defence is to anchor each identity to a scarce, verifiable cost, not free accounts. Before voting or claiming rewards, an agent must post a refundable stake and finish a unique, time-bound task, so creating thousands of fakes multiplies the attacker's expense, not its influence. A thread of attestations ties each identity to its past behaviour, letting peers spot clusters that appear together and vote identically. Like a crystal, trust forms slowly through consistent actions; forging that history takes money, work, and time, making sybil attacks expensive while honest agents stay cheap.
